drafted_from: tool:write-a-public-hosts-paths's row in tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/tool-rows.json, do-work/renew-a-tls-certificate.mjs, do-work/tls-host-owner.py and the tests in test/
start_here: Say to your AI: "Write the public paths of app.example.com on my server at 192.0.2.34, sending everything else to the engine on port 18789." It runs tool:write-a-public-hosts-paths and does not cut any traffic over.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it takes one server's facts as its input and answers what that server's certificate owner reports.
instructions: 1. Gather the server's facts: its public name, IPv4 address, SSH port, the administrator you sign in as, its pinned key ("<address> ssh-ed25519 <key>") and its layout (host: owner path, state folder, downloads folder, ingress, receptionist). The README in tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/ shows a made-up one.

2. Say to your AI the sentence in start_here. It calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:write-a-public-hosts-paths and that input (the worked example shows one). The door mounts your server administration key for the run; you paste no key.

3. Read what comes back: {"public_tls_configured": true, "hostname", "receptionist_configured": true | false, "traffic_cutover": false}; receptionist_configured is true only when you gave receptionistBinary. An {"error": ...} or a thrown message names what to change (for example the layout or the pinned key was refused).
4. remotePort is required (the port the engine's connection listens on). nginx tests the candidate before it replaces the live one. Then run tool:switch-on-a-servers-receptionist.

worked_examples.title: Write the host paths with a receptionist build
worked_examples.ask: Write the public paths for app.example.com.
worked_examples.given: From tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/test/renew-a-tls-certificate.test.mjs (publicProxy keeps /healthz, /download/, the receptionist's four paths to 127.0.0.1:9443 with verified TLS, /privacy and /terms to example.org by GET and HEAD, and every other path to http://127.0.0.1:18789) and test/tls-host-owner.test.py (configure with receptionistBinary answers receptionist_configured true).
